title.en: Reciprocal complex mapping on the Riemann sphere

summary: Relate a bounded complex-plane viewport to the unit sphere and show how reciprocal mapping exchanges zero and infinity.
objective: Drag a complex point through zero using explicit exceptional states and compare z with1/z on linked spheres.
intent_signals: Drag a complex point through zero using explicit exceptional states and compare z with1/z on linked spheres.
Relate a bounded complex-plane viewport to the unit sphere and show how reciprocal mapping exchanges zero and infinity.
example_prompts: Build an explorable reciprocal complex mapping on the riemann sphere. Drag a complex point through zero using explicit exceptional states and compare z with1/z on linked spheres.

entities.name: Equatorial plane and unit sphere
entities.guidance: Use mathematical coordinates(X,Y,Z), sphere centered at0 and plane Z=0. Mark north pole N=(0,0,1), south pole and equator; keep geometric axes equal-scale. The plane is a clipped viewport, not the entire complex plane.

entities.name: Projection construction
entities.guidance: Join N, selected sphere point and finite plane point with one secant. At N replace the finite intersection by an infinity label rather than a very large fake coordinate.

entities.name: Input and output map
entities.guidance: Show matched unit spheres for z and w=1/z with linked labels. In this convention reciprocal mapping sends sphere point(X,Y,Z) to(X,-Y,-Z), a half-turn about X; a finite output panel clips out-of-view values with direction/label.

state_contract.model: For finite z=x+iy, P=(2x,2y,x*x+y*y-1)/(1+x*x+y*y). Inverse z=(X+iY)/(1-Z) for Z!=1. Maintain a tagged infinity value at N. The bounded recipe map is w=1/z with 0 mapped to infinity and infinity mapped to0; use the direct sphere half-turn for these exceptional states.
state_contract.authority: A selected extended-complex value and viewport bounds own both sphere markers and readouts. Spheres use exact unit geometry; visible secants and output-plane clipping are display state, never substitute numerical infinity.
actions: Drag a finite plane point or a sphere point and update both views.
Choose exact zero, one, i and infinity reference states.
Toggle reciprocal mapping and show correspondence without interpolating through an invalid complex division.
Reset point, map selection, viewport and camera independently.

invariants: P has unit norm within declared tolerance; z=0 maps to south pole and |z|=1 to equator.
For finite nonzero z in the display range, applying reciprocal twice returns z within a scale-aware tolerance.
North pole is the one infinity point for every direction; output clipping does not indicate a mathematical singularity except at input zero.
motion_guidance: The sphere half-turn can be animated as an explicitly labeled transition between input and mapped state; intermediate angles are not the function1/z.
Near N, use stable sphere coordinates and a tagged or clipped plane readout rather than overflow or division by a tiny1-Z.
known_limits: This covers one reciprocal map, not arbitrary meromorphic functions, branch cuts, essential singularities or all Mobius transformations.

Finite sphere tessellation and pointer precision cannot resolve an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the pole. Projection is not area-preserving and sphere distances are not complex-plane Euclidean distances.
Authored recipe and prospective checks only; no runtime artifact or rendered result has been observed.

claims.statement: North-pole stereographic projection identifies the unit sphere, apart from(0,0,1), with the complex plane by z=(X+iY)/(1-Z); the north pole represents the single point at infinity of the extended complex plane.
claims.scope: Unit sphere centered at origin, equatorial complex plane, north-pole projection; other sphere conventions differ.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 and 4.4.1 point at infinity; 4.4.2 stereographic projection, PDF indices36-37

object_craft.family: Reciprocal complex mapping on the Riemann sphere
object_craft.structure: Build two sphere grids and an equatorial plane frame with consistent coordinate labels; projection lines meet a shared point rather than near-miss decorative arcs.
object_craft.material: Use independent line weights, shapes and labels for mathematical roles. Color and surface finish are presentation choices; do not infer material physics from them.

creative_affordances: Use wireframe globes, translucent shells or a polished mathematical instrument; allow plane-only inspection alongside the spatial construction.

physical_contract.scope: Derived mathematical geometry and authored inspection; no contact dynamics or calibrated physical artifact.
